item.title: Goldman Sachs cuts gas forecast after ceasefire but warns risks remain
item.description: Goldman Sachs has warned that global natural gas markets face a prolonged supply shock stemming from Iranian attacks on Qatar's liquefied natural gas infrastructure, even as a fragile two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran offers temporary relief. The bank said in an April 2 research note that European gas prices could surge to 75–100 euros per megawatt-hour — roughly double recent levels — if disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz persist beyond April.

item.title: New model suggests dark matter has two particle states
item.description: A team of physicists has put forward a new framework suggesting dark matter may consist of two distinct particle states rather than one, offering a potential explanation for why gamma-ray signals observed at the center of the Milky Way have not appeared in smaller nearby galaxies. The paper, titled "dSph-obic dark matter," was published on Wednesday in the Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics by Asher Berlin, Joshua Foster, Dan Hooper, and Gordan Krnjaic, all affiliated with the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory.

item.title: IUCN lists emperor penguins as endangered over sea ice loss
item.description: The International Union for Conservation of Nature has officially listed emperor penguins as endangered on its Red List of Threatened Species, elevating the iconic Antarctic birds from their previous classification of "near threatened" in a move driven by climate-fueled sea ice loss. The update, announced Thursday, marks one of the most dramatic reclassifications for a polar species in recent years.

item.title: Meta expands CoreWeave deal to $21B, launches Muse Spark AI model
item.description: Meta Platforms made a pair of moves this week to accelerate its artificial intelligence ambitions, launching a new flagship AI model called Muse Spark on Wednesday and announcing a $21 billion cloud computing agreement with CoreWeave on Thursday.

item.title: Chevron projects up to $2.2B Q1 earnings boost from higher oil prices
item.description:
Chevron said on Thursday that higher commodity prices driven by the war in Iran are expected to lift its first-quarter upstream earnings by $1.6 billion to $2.2 billion compared with the fourth quarter of 2025, even as the conflict cut into the company's global production.

The disclosure, made in a regulatory filing, comes a day after rival Exxon Mobil issued a similar update showing the Iran war's dual impact on the world's largest oil producers: surging prices that pad upstream profits, offset by physical disruptions to output across the Persian Gulf.

item.title: UK's Cooper demands toll-free Strait of Hormuz passage
item.description:
British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper is set to declare on Thursday that shipping through the Strait of Hormuz must remain free of tolls, directly challenging both Iran's efforts to control the waterway and a suggestion from President Donald Trump to establish a joint toll system for the critical passage.

In her annual foreign policy address at Mansion House in London, Cooper will argue that international maritime law forbids levying charges on vessels transiting the strait, which carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas.

"The fundamental freedoms of the seas must not be unilaterally withdrawn or sold off to individual bidders. Nor can there be any place for tolls on an international waterway. Freedom of navigation means navigation must be free," Cooper will say, according to advance excerpts of the speech.

item.title: Earth grew 16% brighter at night since 2014, study finds
item.description: Earth's nighttime glow increased by a net 16 percent between 2014 and 2022, according to a study published Wednesday in the journal Nature that also revealed the planet's artificial lighting is far more volatile than scientists previously understood.

item.title: Iran war doubles Russia's oil tax revenue to $9 bn in April
item.description: Russia's revenue from its largest single oil tax is on course to double in April to around $9 billion, according to Reuters calculations published on Thursday, as the global energy crisis triggered by the US and Israeli military campaign against Iran delivers an unexpected financial lifeline to Moscow.

item.title: OpenAI pauses Stargate UK data center over energy costs
item.description: OpenAI announced on Thursday that it is pausing its Stargate artificial intelligence infrastructure project in the United Kingdom, pointing to the high cost of energy and an uncertain regulatory environment as key obstacles to moving forward. The decision deals a blow to the British government's strategy of positioning AI as a driver of economic growth.

item.title: US-Iran ceasefire teeters as Israel bombs Beirut, Hormuz stays blocked
item.description:
A fragile two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran, brokered through last-minute Pakistani mediation, was teetering by its second day on Thursday amid disputes over whether Lebanon is covered by the truce and whether the Strait of Hormuz has truly reopened.

The Associated Press reported Thursday that the ceasefire was "overwhelmed by Israel's heavy bombardment of Beirut, Iran's ongoing grip on the Strait of Hormuz, and doubts regarding whether negotiators can bridge a myriad of other disparities."

item.title: Finland nears launch of world's first permanent nuclear waste site
item.description: After more than two decades of construction, Finland's Onkalo facility is set to become the first site on Earth to permanently dispose of spent nuclear fuel, with authorities expected to grant an operating license within months, according to the Associated Press.

item.title: Oil prices climb again as Strait of Hormuz stays shut despite ceasefire
item.description: The two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran, announced on April 7, has done little to settle global energy and commodity markets, as the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed and oil prices have begun climbing again after an initial sharp selloff.

item.title: Trump demands European warships in Hormuz within days
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is insisting that any German military involvement in securing the Strait of Hormuz must come under an international mandate, setting up a diplomatic standoff with President Donald Trump, who has issued what European diplomats describe as an ultimatum demanding allied warships in the waterway within days.

item.title: Netanyahu orders direct peace talks with Lebanon on Hezbollah
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced Thursday that he had instructed his cabinet to begin direct negotiations with Lebanon "as soon as possible," a move that marks a reversal after Israel previously rebuffed Lebanese overtures for talks.

"In light of Lebanon's repeated requests to open direct negotiations with Israel, I instructed the cabinet yesterday to start direct negotiations with Lebanon as soon as possible," Netanyahu said in a statement, according to Reuters. The negotiations would focus on "disarming Hezbollah and establishing peaceful relations between Israel and Lebanon," he added.

item.title: Iran's nuclear chief rejects enrichment curbs ahead of Islamabad talks
item.description:
Iran's nuclear chief Mohammad Eslami on Thursday dismissed demands to curtail the country's uranium enrichment program, calling such efforts futile just days before high-stakes negotiations with the United States are set to begin in Pakistan's capital.

Speaking on the sidelines of a memorial service marking 40 days since the death of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Eslami said that "the claims and demands of our enemies to restrict Iran's enrichment programme are merely wishes that will be buried," according to Iran's ISNA news agency. He added that no law or external pressure could halt Iran's nuclear progress and that demands to abandon enrichment were "nonsensical".

item.title: UK forces Russian submarines to retreat from undersea cables
item.description:
Britain on Thursday revealed it had tracked three Russian submarines conducting covert operations near undersea cables and pipelines in waters north of the UK, in a month-long surveillance campaign that ended with all three vessels retreating toward Russia.

Defence Secretary John Healey said British forces identified an Akula-class nuclear attack submarine entering international waters in the High North several weeks ago and quickly determined it was deployed as a distraction while two submarines from Russia's Main Directorate of Deep Sea Research, known as GUGI, carried out what the Ministry of Defence described as "nefarious activity" near critical underwater infrastructure.

item.title: Iran demands Bitcoin tolls for Hormuz tanker passage
item.description: Despite a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran announced Tuesday evening, Tehran is pressing ahead with demands that oil tankers pay tolls in Bitcoin and other digital currencies to transit the Strait of Hormuz, raising doubts about whether the critical waterway will see a meaningful return of commercial shipping anytime soon.

item.title: Iran envoy deletes post on Islamabad delegation amid ceasefire rift
item.description:
Iran's Ambassador to Pakistan, Reza Amiri Moghadam, deleted a post on X late Thursday announcing that an Iranian delegation would arrive in Islamabad that evening for talks with the United States, raising fresh uncertainty about whether high-stakes negotiations set for Friday will go ahead as planned.

Moghadam had written that "despite skepticism of Iranian public opinion due to repeated ceasefire violations by Israeli regime to sabotage the diplomatic initiative," the delegation would arrive Thursday night at the invitation of Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for "serious talks based on 10 points proposed by Iran," according to Moneycontrol, which published the text of the post before it was removed. The post was subsequently deleted, Xinhua International reported, though no official explanation was given.

item.title: Netanyahu rejects cease-fire calls, vows strikes on Hezbollah
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reiterated on Thursday that there is no ceasefire in Lebanon, defying international calls to extend a fragile US-Iran truce to cover Israeli military operations against Hezbollah. In a video message, Netanyahu declared, "There is no ceasefire. We are continuing to hit Hezbollah with force and we will not stop until we restore security," while also directing his cabinet to pursue direct negotiations with the Lebanese government aimed at disarming the militant group.

The statement came a day after Israel carried out its deadliest wave of strikes on Lebanon since the broader conflict began in early March, with the Israeli military saying it hit more than 100 Hezbollah command centers and military sites across Beirut, the Bekaa Valley, and southern Lebanon in just 10 minutes. Lebanon's health ministry reported at least 254 people killed and over 1,165 wounded in Wednesday's attacks, according to Al Jazeera. Several strikes hit densely populated commercial and residential areas in central Beirut without prior warning.

item.title: Trump says he's 'very optimistic' on Iran deal amid Lebanon crisis
item.description:
President Trump said Thursday he was "very optimistic" about securing a peace deal with Iran, even as massive Israeli strikes on Lebanon threatened to unravel a fragile ceasefire between Washington and Tehran that is only days old.

In a telephone interview with NBC News, Trump said Iranian leaders were "much more reasonable" in private negotiations than in their public statements, according to AFP. He added a warning: "If they don't make a deal, it's going to be very painful".
